summary: Show a stimulus for a controlled duration, then hide it and ask about it. Concept and pack tests.
use_when: exposure time is part of the method
the stimulus must be hidden before the questions
the request mentions timed, forced or controlled exposure
warnings: Interview only in this release. Scaffold from `basic`, then apply this archetype's questions and capture shape by hand; `basic` is the reference structure and every archetype inherits it.

questions.ask: How long is the exposure, and is it fixed by us or set per survey?
questions.why: If a designer sets it, it is public API and needs a sane default and a documented range.

questions.ask: What happens if the respondent's browser throttles the timer, for example on a background tab?
questions.why: A background tab throttles timers, so a wall-clock exposure and an intended exposure diverge. The actual elapsed time must be captured, not assumed.

questions.ask: Is re-exposure allowed, and if so how many times?
questions.why: Re-exposure changes the measure, so each exposure needs its own timestamped record.

questions.ask: What must the respondent not be able to do: screenshot, right-click, go back?
questions.why: These protections range from cosmetic to termination-inducing. The reference implementation shipped a security layer whose termination code was unmapped, so it force-advanced respondents mid-stimulus instead of terminating them.
